 With only four games on the menu tonight for NBA fans, value plays and picks will be more concentrated. However, prediction markets like ProphetX are still one of the best ways for hoops fans to get more involved.
 The slate begins on the East Coast, when Tyrese Maxey and the Philadelphia 76ers host the Toronto Raptors. The Sixers are coming off their second 20-point loss in the last three games, and LeBron James and Joel Embiid may sit out this contest since it's the second game of a back-to-back.

 The Washington Wizards are hoping to snap their five-game losing streak tonight when they host the Detroit Pistons. Anthony Davis had one of his best games in recent memory with a 44-point, 13-rebound performance on Monday against Detroit, but his team still couldn't find a way to win.
 LaMelo Ball and the Minnesota Timberwolves will take on the surprising Dallas Mavericks at Target Center. Both teams in this bout are riding win streaks, but one of those has to end tonight. And the night will conclude when the Charlotte Hornets start their Western Conference road trip against the Phoenix Suns in The Valley. Charlotte will have to play without Brandon Miller and Kon Knueppel due to injuries, but they were able to suffice without them against Cleveland with a 124-112 win.
 With the NBA season back in action, now is the perfect time to get started with ProphetX. New users can get started with the  TSN   promo code for a $40 prediction bonus . The Sporting News has everything you need to know about Thursday night's NBA slate, along with how to get $40 worth of prediction bonuses on ProphetX.

 NBA markets on ProphetX
 ProphetX has an extensive selection of available markets for NBA action. As a reminder for those used to sports betting, ProphetX displays market percentages instead of betting odds. The percentages reflect the collective implied probability of an event. Meanwhile, betting odds are set by the house to bake in a profit margin.
 Here's an outline of some markets users can predict on:

 NBA value picks for Thursday
 Pistons -10.5 vs. Wizards  ( 50.98% on ProphetX )
 Things have taken a turn for the worse in Washington after starting the season 4-3. Since then, the Wizards have been on a five-game skid, and four of those losses have come by 11 points or more. That's the exact margin of victory Detroit won with on Monday against this same Washington side. Additionally, the Pistons haven't played a game since then, a statement Anthony Davis and Co. cannot agree with. His team is coming off a frustrating 13-point loss to the Tyrese Haliburton-less Pacers.
 There are just too many advantages leaning Detroit's way: rest, talent, offensive and defensive statistics. Despite having Davis, Trae Young, and rookie AJ Dybantsa, the Wizards have been having a tough time scoring points this season. They're averaging a fourth-lowest 107.5 PPG, and the Pistons' third-ranked defense is likely salivating with this matchup.
 76ers vs. Raptors under 222.5 points  ( 47.62% on ProphetX )
 Basketball fans in the loop may pick up on something that could point towards this game going under. LeBron James and Joel Embiid are currently questionable with various injuries. That being said, Philadelphia is coming off a tolling 22-point loss to Jayson Tatum and the Celtics, so this could just be a load management game for Nick Nurse's crew. Toronto has also been shorthanded due to a slew of injuries of their own. Scottie Barnes has sat out of the last three contests with an adductor/groin injury, and Kawhi Leonard only played two games before going down with a left knee injury.
 When Philadelphia last rested James and Embiid against the Hornets, the two sides combined for only 213 points. A scoreline that mirrors this previous effort is easy to visualize for tonight, so don't be afraid to take the under here.
 Timberwolves -5.5 vs. Mavericks  ( 52.61% on ProphetX )
 Minnesota enters the second game of their homestand on a four-game winning streak, along with wins in five of their last six games. The Wolves, even despite the absence of star Anthony Edwards, are the top rebounding team in the league with 48.8 per game. Ayo Dosunmu has been stepping up in light of Edwards' absence with averages of 18.1 PPG, 4.9 RPG, and 4.0 APG.
 The Timberwolves also carry a 4-1 home record this season, and they have shot nearly 50% from the floor when playing at Target Center. Dallas is also on a three-game win streak, but those wins came against struggling teams like Utah, Brooklyn, and Indiana. Minnesota has a slight edge here, and they should be able to cover this spread for a fifth straight game.

 NBA player props for Thursday
 Tyrese Maxey over 24.5 points  ( 50.98% on ProphetX )
 This line has exquisite value for a player who has performed as well as Maxey has against Toronto in the past. Last season, he averaged 31.5 points in the four games versus the Raptors. He went over this line in three of the four games, with the sole outlier being a 24-point outing. The absence of James and Embiid would mean even more scoring is on the table for Maxey, as he tallied 38 points when they sat out against Charlotte on Oct. 31. He should smash this line tonight.
 Anthony Davis over 32.5 points + rebounds  ( 53.92% on ProphetX )
 This line may be a bit overinflated after Davis dropped 44 points and 13 rebounds against Detroit earlier this week, but that shouldn't be a problem. Washington's big man is averaging top-15 marks with his 25.2 PPG and 10.0 RPG. He's hit this line in five straight games in which he has played. The Pistons opted to start John Collins as their starting center; if J.B. Bickerstaff opts to start with small ball again, Davis should be in for a big night. Washington needs to snap their losing streak eventually, and they'll need their star big to ball.
 Grayson Allen over 2.5 threes  ( 69.23% on ProphetX )
 The Hornets have had a tough break since the end of last season after they traded away LaMelo Ball, and they've had to deal with early injuries to Brandon Miller, Kon Knueppel, and Dennis Schroder. Grayson Allen has been one of the players to pick up more of a workload these last few games as the team's premier sharpshooter.
 He's shot 7.4 three-pointers per game this season (23rd in the NBA) and is coming off a big night where he hit six against Cleveland. Allen has gone over this 2.5 threes line in four of the last five games, and Miller's absence last game specifically showed what the former Duke Blue Devil can do when his team is short-handed. This line of 2.5 is a safer play, just because Allen has had his off nights in the past, but confident users can also take his over on 3.5 threes for  46.51% on ProphetX .
